dek: Kings Creek Falls is the Lassen Volcanic waterfall we cover, a 1.1-mile one-way hike. The entrance fee drops from $30 to $10 in winter, when trails are under snow.
overview: Lassen Volcanic National Park is a volcanic landscape of fumaroles, wildflower meadows and hot water that is still shaping the ground.

Kings Creek Falls is the waterfall we cover here. It is on Kings Creek, near the town of Chester. Our trail file puts the hike at 1.1 miles one way and gives it a T2 mountain-hiking rating. The park's weather page says the trails snow over in winter and melt out in spring, and that crews dig the main road out from 30 to 40 feet of snow each year.
fallsIntro: Kings Creek Falls is the only waterfall we list in the park. The trail file gives a one-way distance and a hiking rating but no elevation gain.
plan: The outing is Kings Creek Falls, 1.1 miles one way. A calendar date isn't the same as an open trailhead here: the park clears 30 to 40 feet of snow off the main road every spring, and the trail may not be melted out until then.
feesLead: The vehicle fee is $30 from April 16 through November 30 and $10 from December 1 through April 15. The cheaper window is when the trails are under snow.
access: When the entrance station isn't staffed, the fee page says you can buy a digital pass online. The pages we checked don't describe a timed-entry system. Chester is the nearest town in our index, about 15 miles away in a straight line, but that is a town label rather than the Kings Creek trailhead.
safety: The hazard on file is seasonal access rather than a cliff: snow on the trails in winter, melt in spring, and a main road that starts the year under 30 to 40 feet of snow. The trail carries a T2 mountain-hiking rating.
